subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Granite: The Stone That Lasts Forever
description: A quick win: understand Granite: The Stone That Lasts Forever.

hook.text: The faces on Mount Rushmore erode 1 inch every 10,000 years. They'll be recognizable for millennia.

buildup.text: Granite forms deep underground from slowly cooling magma. Its interlocking crystals make it incredibly hard.

discovery.text: Granite's compressive strength is about 200 MPa — seven times stronger than concrete.

twist.text: Egyptians cut granite with copper tools and sand. The process took months for a single obelisk.

climax.text: Today, diamond-tipped saws cut granite in minutes. Countertops cost more than ancient temples did.

punchline.text: Stone that outlasts civilizations. Now it holds your coffee.

quiz.question: How much stronger is granite compared to concrete?
options: About twice as strong in compression tests
About seven times stronger in compression
They are roughly equal in strength
